name: Mattenai
overview: Mattenai was a male member of the tribe of Levi, identified specifically as the son of Joiarib. As a descendant of Aaron, he belonged to the priestly line, serving in the capacity of a priest as noted in Nehemiah 12:19. His role within the Levitical priesthood highlights his participation in the religious leadership of Israel during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattenai means "gift," reflecting a proper name without indication of divine bestowal. This meaning emphasizes the concept of being a gift, though the Scripture does not explicitly connect this to his character or role beyond the literal name meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Mattenai was the son of Joiarib, establishing his lineage within the priestly family. No additional family relationships are documented beyond this father-son connection.
scriptureSignificance: Mattenai's significance lies in his identification as a priest descended from Aaron, which situates him within the sacred Levitical ministry responsible for temple worship and religious duties. His mention in Nehemiah 12:19 places him among those who contributed to the restoration and organization of the priesthood following the return from exile, underscoring the continuity of God's covenantal priestly line.
